pages.title: The City and the Age
pages.content:
Islam started in the 7th century in the city of Mecca. The period before Islam was called the Age of Ignorance, or Jahiliyyah because religious and social disorder was common in society. Life was hard and chaotic. There was no central government in Arabia, and tribes were the basis of society.

Before Islam, Mecca was led by a council of rich merchants. For this reason, the city was known as the Republic of Merchants. Powerful people controlled many parts of life, while poor and weak people lived in misery.

Society was not fair, and people from poor backgrounds were often treated badly. The Qur’an describes this period as a time of ignorance and cruelty. Violence, hatred, and fighting were common in the social life of the time.

exercises.title: The Age of Ignorance
exercises.instructions: Read the question. Choose the answer from Chapter 1.
exercises.question: Why was the period before Islam called the Age of Ignorance, or Jahiliyyah?
options: A council of rich merchants led the city of Mecca.
Religious and social disorder was common in society.
Mecca had no trade with other places.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 1 says the period “was called the Age of Ignorance, or Jahiliyyah because religious and social disorder was common in society.” The council of rich merchants explains a different name: The Republic of Merchants.

feedback.correct: Right. The word “because” in the first paragraph links the name to religious and social disorder.
feedback.incorrect: Read the first paragraph again and find the word “because” after “Jahiliyyah”. The merchants explain a different name.

languageFocusExercises.title: What Does “This Reason” Point To?
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Read the two sentences from Chapter 1. Then choose the best answer.
languageFocusExercises.question: “Before Islam, Mecca was led by a council of rich merchants. For this reason, the city was known as the Republic of Merchants.” What is “this reason”?
options: Islam started in the 7th century in Mecca.
A council of rich merchants led Mecca.
Poor and weak people lived in misery.
There was no central government in Arabia.
languageFocusExercises.explanation: “For this reason” points back to the sentence just before it and introduces a result. Mecca was led by rich merchants, so people called it the Republic of Merchants. Writers use “this reason”, “this period” or “this city” to connect a new sentence to an idea they have already given.

feedback.correct: Correct. The name “Republic of Merchants” is a result of who led the city.
feedback.incorrect: Read the sentence directly before “For this reason” in the second paragraph. Which fact explains the name “Republic of Merchants”?

languageFocusExercises.title: Reason or Contrast?
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Complete the lines from Chapter 1 with words from the bank. Two words are not needed.
languageFocusExercises.question: Which word gives a reason, and which word puts two different situations side by side?
languageFocusExercises.fillBlanksText: The period before Islam was called the Age of Ignorance, or Jahiliyyah, [blank] religious and social disorder was common in society. … Powerful people controlled many parts of life, [blank] poor and weak people lived in misery.
languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Because” + subject + verb gives the reason for the name: disorder was common. “While” can put two situations that existed at the same time side by side to show a contrast: The powerful controlled life, but the poor and weak suffered. “Because of” and “during” need a noun, not a full clause (subject + verb).

feedback.correct: Correct. “Because” explains the name, and “while” contrasts the two groups.
feedback.incorrect: Ask: Does the second part explain why, or does it show a different group at the same time? Then check the first two paragraphs of Chapter 1.

languageFocusExercises.title: Who Did It, and Who Says So?
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Rewrite each sentence so that it keeps the same meaning. Use the start that is given.
languageFocusExercises.question: How else can we say these sentences from Chapter 1?

transformItems.source: Society was not fair, and people from poor backgrounds were often treated badly.
transformItems.frame: Society was not fair, and others often [blank] badly.
answers: treated people from a poor background

transformItems.source: The Qur’an describes this period as a time of ignorance and cruelty.
transformItems.frame: In the Qur’an, this period [blank] a time of ignorance and cruelty.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: The chapter uses the passive (“were often treated badly”) because the people who suffered are the focus, and the doers are general or unknown. Your active version needs a vague subject such as “others”, which shows why the passive sounds better here. “X describes Y as Z” names the source of a description; the passive “Y is described as Z in X” keeps the same source but puts the period first.

feedback.correct: Well done. You moved between active and passive and kept the source of the description clear.
feedback.incorrect: Item 1: put the affected people after the active verb “treated”. Item 2: use is/was + “described as”. Check the last paragraph of Chapter 1.

languageFocusExercises.title: Write a Connected Historical Snapshot
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Write or say five or six sentences about another city or people from history.
languageFocusExercises.question: What was life like there, and why?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: A strong answer should read like one short historical paragraph rather than separate grammar examples. Useful patterns include “In the ... century...”, “was called... because...”, “for this reason...”, “while...”, “was led by...”, and “X describes... as...”.

feedback.correct: Keep the ideas connected so the paragraph develops one historical situation clearly.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 1 — Give the time and place.
discussionPrompts.example: In the 19th century, many people moved to the growing factory towns of England.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 2 — Say who led the city or how people lived.
discussionPrompts.example: There were few laws to protect workers, and children often worked long hours.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 3 — Give a reason with “because” or a result with “For this reason, …”
discussionPrompts.example: Factory owners wanted cheap workers. For this reason, many poor families sent their children to work.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 4 — Compare two groups with “while”.
discussionPrompts.example: The owners lived in large, comfortable houses, while the workers lived in small, crowded rooms.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentences 5–6 — Add “… were often treated …” or “… was known as …”
discussionPrompts.example: Many workers were treated badly in the factories. Writers of that time describe the streets as dirty and unhealthy.

pages.title: The Age of Ignorance
pages.content:
The Jahiliyyah was an age of barbarism. People did not truly know Allah, and many people did not have justice, order, and peace in their personal and social lives. Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) described Islam as the opposite of barbarism. This era ended when the first revelation of the Qur’an began in 610 CE.

To understand the Jahiliyyah period, we must first talk about Mecca. Mecca is the holy city of Islam. Allah chose this city to be the location of His House, the Holy Ka’ba.

Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) was also born in Mecca. He spent 52 years of his life in this city and began to teach the message of Islam here. The Qiblah, the direction Muslims face during salah, is also located in Mecca.

exercises.title: The End of an Era
exercises.instructions: Is the sentence true or false? Use Chapter 2.
exercises.question: The Jahiliyyah era ended when Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) was born in Mecca.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 2 says: “This era ended when the first revelation of the Qur’an began in 610 CE.” The Prophet’s (pbuh) birth in Mecca is mentioned later, in the last paragraph, but it is not the end of the era.

feedback.correct: Correct. The era ended with the first revelation of the Qur’an in 610 CE, not with the Prophet’s (pbuh) birth.
feedback.incorrect: Look at the last sentence of the first paragraph: What began in 610 CE and ended the era?

languageFocusExercises.title: Follow the Explanation
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Put the sentences from Chapter 2 in order. Words like “first” and “this city” help.
languageFocusExercises.question: How does the writer move from the Jahiliyyah to a short profile of Mecca?

sequencingItems.text: Allah chose this city to be the location of His House, the Holy Ka’ba.
Mecca is the holy city of Islam.
The Jahiliyyah was an age of barbarism.
To understand the Jahiliyyah period, we must first talk about Mecca.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: The writer first defines the period (“The Jahiliyyah was an age of barbarism”). “To understand the Jahiliyyah period, we must first …” refers back to that period and states the purpose and the first step of the next explanation. Then the new topic, Mecca, is introduced with a short definition. “This city” refers back to Mecca, so it must come after Mecca has been named.

feedback.correct: Correct. Definition of the period, purpose and first step, the new topic, then a sentence that refers back to it.
feedback.incorrect: Start with the sentence that defines the period. Then ask: Which sentence says what we must do first, which names Mecca, and which refers back to “this city”?

languageFocusExercises.title: Describing One Idea as Another
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Tap the pieces to rebuild this sentence from Chapter 2.
languageFocusExercises.question: Where does “as” go when we describe one idea in terms of another?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: The pattern is describe + thing + as + description: “described Islam as the opposite of barbarism”. The same pattern appears in Chapter 1: “The Qur’an describes this period as a time of ignorance and cruelty.” Here the pattern builds a contrast because the chapter has just called the Jahiliyyah “an age of barbarism”.

feedback.correct: Well done. The thing being described comes straight after “described”, and “as” introduces the description.
feedback.incorrect: Start with the person, then “described”, then what he described, then “as …”. Check the first paragraph of Chapter 2.

languageFocusExercises.title: Time Clauses and Inserted Definitions
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Rewrite each sentence so that it keeps the same meaning. Use the start that is given.
languageFocusExercises.question: How else can we say these sentences from Chapter 2?

transformItems.source: This era ended when the first revelation of the Qur’an began in 610 CE.
transformItems.frame: When the first revelation of the Qur’an began in 610 CE, [blank].

transformItems.source: The Qiblah, the direction Muslims face during salah, is also located in Mecca.
transformItems.frame: The Qiblah is also located in Mecca. It is [blank] during salah.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: A “when” clause can come after or before the main clause. When it comes first, we put a comma after it. A noun phrase between commas (“the Qiblah, the direction Muslims face during salah, …”) defines the word just before it. The writer puts the definition inside the sentence so the reader understands the term and gets a new fact at the same time.

feedback.correct: Well done. You moved the time clause and turned the inserted definition into its own sentence.
feedback.incorrect: Item 1: after the comma, add the main clause about the era. Item 2: use the words between the commas in the last sentence of Chapter 2.

languageFocusExercises.title: Build a Short Explanatory Profile
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Write or say five or six sentences about another important city or place.
languageFocusExercises.question: What is this place, and why is it important?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: A strong response should use connected explanatory language such as “To understand..., we must first...”, “is...”, “also”, “and”, and a short inserted definition like “X, the..., ...”.

feedback.correct: Keep the paragraph focused on one topic and make each added detail support the explanation.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 1 — Define or characterize the place/institution.
discussionPrompts.example: The old library in our city is a public place where everyone can read and study for free.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 2 — Explain why the reader needs to understand it.
discussionPrompts.example: Readers need to understand it because it shows how our city cared about learning.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 3 — Use “must first” or another clear ordering expression.
discussionPrompts.example: To understand the library, we must first look at the history of the old city.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 4 — Add a related fact with “also”.
discussionPrompts.example: The library also has a small museum with very old books.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 5–6 — Join related information and define one key term inside a sentence.
discussionPrompts.example: It stands near the main square, the center of the old city. Its reading room, a large hall with long tables, is the most popular part.

pages.title: The Beginning of Mecca
pages.content:
The Qur’an describes Mecca as a valley where no crops grow. City life began there with the building of the Ka’ba. When Prophet Abraham (pbuh) brought his son Ishmael (pbuh) and his wife Hagar to the city, Zamzam water had not been discovered yet. There was no population in the land.

After the discovery of Zamzam water, the Jurhumites from Yemen settled in Mecca. Ishmael (pbuh) learned Arabic from them. Later, when Ishmael (pbuh) grew up, Abraham (pbuh) came to the city to build the Holy Ka’ba again with his son.

Arabs accepted the religion of Abraham (pbuh) and Ishmael (pbuh), so the Ka’ba became a pilgrimage site. This helped the city grow rapidly.

exercises.title: From Valley to City
exercises.instructions: Put the events from Chapter 3 in the right order.
exercises.question: How did an empty valley become a growing city?

sequencingItems.text: Abraham (pbuh) brought Ishmael (pbuh) and Hagar to a land with no population.
Zamzam water was discovered.
The Jurhumites from Yemen settled in Mecca.
Abraham (pbuh) and his son built the Holy Ka’ba again.
The Ka’ba became a pilgrimage site, and the city grew rapidly.

exercises.explanation: When Abraham (pbuh) brought his family, “Zamzam water had not been discovered yet.” “After the discovery of Zamzam water, the Jurhumites from Yemen settled in Mecca.” Later Abraham (pbuh) and Ishmael (pbuh) built the Ka’ba again, it became a pilgrimage site, and “this helped the city grow rapidly.”

feedback.correct: Well done. Each step made the next one possible: water, people, the Ka’ba, then pilgrims and growth.
feedback.incorrect: Look for the time words in Chapter 3: “had not been discovered yet”, “After the discovery …”, “Later, when Ishmael (pbuh) grew up …”, and the result in the last paragraph.

languageFocusExercises.title: Which Came First?
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Read the sentence from Chapter 3. What does it tell us about the order?
languageFocusExercises.question: “When Prophet Abraham (pbuh) brought his son Ishmael (pbuh) and his wife Hagar to the city, Zamzam water had not been discovered yet.” What does “had not been discovered yet” tell us?
options: Zamzam water was discovered before they arrived.
Zamzam water was discovered at the moment they arrived.
Zamzam water was discovered some time after they arrived.
languageFocusExercises.explanation: The past perfect (had + been + past participle) looks back from one past moment to an earlier time. At the moment of arrival, the discovery had not happened; “yet” shows that people expected it to happen later. The next paragraph confirms this: “After the discovery of Zamzam water, the Jurhumites from Yemen settled in Mecca.”

feedback.correct: Correct. At the time of their arrival, the discovery was still in the future.
feedback.incorrect: Think about “not … yet”: something has not happened so far, but may happen later. Then read the start of the second paragraph of Chapter 3.

languageFocusExercises.title: Reason and Result, Noun and Clause
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Rewrite each sentence so that it keeps the same meaning. Use the start that is given.
languageFocusExercises.question: How else can we say these sentences from Chapter 3?

transformItems.source: Arabs accepted the religion of Abraham (pbuh) and Ishmael (pbuh), so the Ka’ba became a pilgrimage site.
transformItems.frame: The Ka’ba became a pilgrimage site [blank] the religion of Abraham (pbuh) and Ishmael (pbuh).

transformItems.source: After the discovery of Zamzam water, the Jurhumites from Yemen settled in Mecca.
transformItems.frame: After Zamzam water [blank], the Jurhumites from Yemen settled in Mecca.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: “So” introduces a result; “because”, “as” or “since” introduce a reason. When you change the order of the ideas, you change the linker. “After” can be followed by a noun (“after the discovery”) or by a clause (“after Zamzam water was discovered”). The water is the thing that was found, so the clause is passive.

feedback.correct: Well done. You kept the same cause and effect and the same order of events.
feedback.incorrect: Item 1: which part is the reason? Start the gap with “because”. Item 2: the water did not discover anything; it was found by people, so use was/had been + discovered.

languageFocusExercises.title: Place, Purpose and Growth
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Choose the correct form to complete each sentence from Chapter 3.
languageFocusExercises.question: Which form describes a place, gives a purpose and shows help with a change?

formChoices.sentence: The Qur’an describes Mecca as a valley [choice] no crops grow.
Later, when Ishmael (pbuh) grew up, Abraham (pbuh) came to the city [choice] the Holy Ka’ba again with his son.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Where” adds information about a place: in this valley, no crops grow. (“Which” would need a subject or object, as in “a valley which has no crops”.) “To + verb” gives the purpose of an action: Why did Abraham come? To build the Ka’ba again. “Help + object + base verb” shows that one thing supported a change: pilgrimage helped the city grow.

feedback.correct: Correct. You chose the right form for place, purpose and growth.
feedback.incorrect: Ask: Does the gap describe a place, answer “why?”, or follow “helped the city”? Then check the first and last paragraphs of Chapter 3.

languageFocusExercises.title: Explain How a Place Changed Over Time
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Write or say six sentences about another place that changed over time.
languageFocusExercises.question: What was the place like, and how did it change?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: A strong response should form one short historical paragraph. Useful patterns include “a place where...”, “There was/were...”, “had not ... yet”, “after...”, “later, when...”, “to + verb”, “so...”, and “helped ... grow/change”.

feedback.correct: Keep the time relationships clear and make each sentence move the explanation forward.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 1 — Describe the place with “where” or another defining phrase.
discussionPrompts.example: Our town began as a small village where fishermen lived by the sea.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 2 — State an earlier condition that existed before change.
discussionPrompts.example: Before the railway arrived, very few visitors came to the village.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 3 — Use “after” to introduce the next development.
discussionPrompts.example: After the railway was built, traders started to bring their goods to the little port.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 4 — Use “later, when...” to move to another stage.
discussionPrompts.example: Later, when the port became busy, families from other towns moved there.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 5 — Explain the purpose of one action with “to + verb”.
discussionPrompts.example: The town built a new school to teach the children of these families.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 6 — Finish with a result using “so” or “helped ... change”.
discussionPrompts.example: So the small village grew into a busy town, and the railway helped it change.

pages.title: The Ka’ba and Trade
pages.content:
After Abraham (pbuh) completed his mission and invited people for pilgrimage, he returned to Palestine. Later, the Khuza’a tribe came to Mecca, defeated the Jurhum tribe, and took control of the city.

Under Khuza’a rule, people forgot the religion of Abraham (pbuh) and started worshipping many idols. Later, in the 5th century, the Quraysh tribe took over the city and the Ka’ba.

Because people could not farm in this dry land, they made money through trade. When Islam began, the Byzantine and Sassanid empires were powerful states. They traded with both the north and south of Arabia. India, Indonesia, and China were also important for trade because they produced many different goods.

exercises.title: Who Did What?
exercises.instructions: Match each person or group with what Chapter 4 says about them.
exercises.question: Who did what in Chapter 4?

matchingPairs.right: returned to Palestine after inviting people for pilgrimage
defeated the Jurhum tribe and took control of Mecca
took over the city and the Ka’ba in the 5th century
could not farm the dry land, so they made money through trade

correctAnswer.Abraham (pbuh): returned to Palestine after inviting people for pilgrimage
correctAnswer.The Khuza’a tribe: defeated the Jurhum tribe and took control of Mecca
correctAnswer.The Quraysh tribe: took over the city and the Ka’ba in the 5th century
correctAnswer.The people of Mecca: could not farm the dry land, so they made money through trade

exercises.explanation: Chapter 4 follows the changes of control in Mecca: Abraham (pbuh) “returned to Palestine”, the Khuza’a tribe “defeated the Jurhum tribe”, and “in the 5th century, the Quraysh tribe took over the city and the Ka’ba.” It also says: “Because people could not farm in this dry land, they made money through trade.”

feedback.correct: Great. You followed who controlled Mecca and why its people turned to trade.
feedback.incorrect: The first two paragraphs tell you who came, who left and who took control. The last paragraph explains how people made money.

languageFocusExercises.title: Stages of Control
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Put the parts of Chapter 4 in time order. The time words will help you.
languageFocusExercises.question: How do “after”, “later” and “under … rule” guide the reader through the changes in Mecca?

sequencingItems.text: Later, in the 5th century, the Quraysh tribe …
Under Khuza’a rule, people forgot the religion of Abraham (pbuh) …
After Abraham (pbuh) completed his mission and invited people for pilgrimage, he returned to Palestine.
Later, the Khuza’a tribe came to Mecca, defeated the Jurhum tribe, and took control of the city.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: “After …” closes one stage before the next begins. “Later” moves the account forward, and “Later, in the 5th century” adds an exact time. “Under Khuza’a rule” describes life during a period of control, so it must come after the Khuza’a took control. A history text often uses these markers to show a chain of rulers and changes.

feedback.correct: Correct. You followed the time markers from Abraham to the Quraysh.
feedback.incorrect: Start with the sentence that closes Abraham’s stage. “Under Khuza’a rule” can only come after the Khuza’a took control.

languageFocusExercises.title: Starting and Taking Over
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Choose the correct form to complete each sentence from Chapter 4.
languageFocusExercises.question: Which forms show the start of a new practice and a new group taking control?

formChoices.sentence: … people forgot the religion of Abraham (pbuh) and started [choice] many idols.
Later, in the 5th century, the Quraysh tribe took [choice] the city and the Ka’ba.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Start” is followed by -ing (or to + verb) to show the beginning of an action: “started worshipping”. “Take over” is a phrasal verb meaning “take control of”; the chapter uses both “took control of the city” and “took over the city”. “Take off” and “take up” have very different meanings.

feedback.correct: Correct. You showed the start of a practice and a change of control.
feedback.incorrect: After “started”, use a form that can follow it as an object. For the second gap, which small word means “took control of”? Check the second paragraph of Chapter 4.

languageFocusExercises.title: Reason First or Reason Second?
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Rewrite each sentence so that it keeps the same meaning. Use the start that is given.
languageFocusExercises.question: Where else can the reason go in these sentences?

transformItems.source: Because people could not farm in this dry land, they made money through trade.
transformItems.frame: People made money through trade [blank] farm in this dry land.
answers: because they were not able to

transformItems.source: India, Indonesia, and China were also important for trade because they produced many different goods.
transformItems.frame: India, Indonesia, and China produced many different goods, [blank] important for trade.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: A “because” clause can come first (with a comma) or second (without a comma). “Could not + verb” shows what was impossible, and the main clause shows what people did instead. If the reason comes first as a full sentence part, use “so” to introduce the result.

feedback.correct: Well done. You kept the same reason and result in a new order.
feedback.incorrect: Item 1: start the gap with “because” and keep “could not”. Item 2: the goods are the reason, so start the gap with “so”.

languageFocusExercises.title: Explain a Historical Change
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Write or say six sentences about another place or community that changed.
languageFocusExercises.question: Who controlled the place, and what changed?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: A strong response should form one connected paragraph. Useful patterns include “after...”, “later...”, “under ... rule...”, “started + -ing”, “because ... could not..., ...”, and “when ... began, ... was/were ...”.

feedback.correct: Keep the sequence clear and make each connector show a real relationship between ideas.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 1 — Close an earlier stage with “after...”.
discussionPrompts.example: After the old bridge fell down, our village was cut off from the town for many years.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 2 — Introduce a later change with “later...”.
discussionPrompts.example: Later, a new mayor came and built a stronger bridge.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 3 — Describe life “under” a new period or authority.
discussionPrompts.example: Under the new mayor, people traveled to the town every week.

pages.title: The Trade Routes
pages.content:
Because Mecca was in the middle of important trade routes, it became a busy and wealthy city. From the early 6th century, Mecca became a major trading center.

Hashim ibn Abd Manaf, Prophet Muhammad’s (pbuh) great-grandfather, helped grow Mecca’s economy. He and the Quraysh leaders made special trade agreements with other tribes and nations. These agreements allowed merchants to travel safely and trade in places like Byzantium, Yemen, Iraq, and Ethiopia.

The sacred months, Dhu al-Qadah, Dhu al-Hijjah, Muharram, and Rajab, made the region safer. In these months, people focused on worship, showed respect, and stayed away from fighting. Because of this safe atmosphere, more people could visit the city to perform Hajj.

exercises.title: Safe Months
exercises.instructions: Read the question. Choose the answer from Chapter 5.
exercises.question: Why could more people visit Mecca to perform Hajj?
options: Mecca was far from the busy trade routes, so the roads were quiet and easy to travel.
In the sacred months people stayed away from fighting, so the region was safer.
The Quraysh leaders stopped all trade during the pilgrimage season, so the city was quiet.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 5 says the sacred months “made the region safer. In these months, people focused on worship, showed respect, and stayed away from fighting. Because of this safe atmosphere, more people could visit the city to perform Hajj.”

feedback.correct: Right. The sacred months made the region safe, and this safe atmosphere brought more pilgrims.
feedback.incorrect: Read the last paragraph of Chapter 5 and find the words “Because of this …”. What made the region safer?

languageFocusExercises.title: “Because” or “Because of”?
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Compare the two sentences from Chapter 5. Then choose the best answer.
languageFocusExercises.question: (1) “Because Mecca was in the middle of important trade routes, it became a busy and wealthy city.” (2) “Because of this safe atmosphere, more people could visit the city …” Why does the writer use “because” in (1) but “because of” in (2)?
options: “Because” gives a reason, but “because of” gives a result of the safe atmosphere in the city.
“Because” is followed by a subject and a verb; “because of” is followed by a noun phrase.
“Because of” can only be used at the start of a sentence, and “because” can only be used in the middle.
There is no difference; the writer only wanted some variety.
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Both give a reason. The difference is what follows: “because + subject + verb” (Mecca was …) and “because of + noun phrase” (this safe atmosphere). Both can start a sentence or come in the middle. The two sentences frame the chapter: Location made Mecca rich, and safety brought more visitors.

feedback.correct: Correct. Look at what comes straight after each one: A clause or a noun phrase.
feedback.incorrect: Both sentences explain why something happened. Now look at the words straight after “because” and after “because of”. Is there a verb?

languageFocusExercises.title: What Do These Phrases Mean?
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Match each phrase from Chapter 5 with its meaning.
languageFocusExercises.question: What do these phrases tell us about trade and behavior in and around Mecca?

matchingPairs.right: played a part in making the city’s business bigger
made it possible for traders to go on journeys
gave most of their attention to prayer and religious acts
treated others with honor
avoided war and violence

correctAnswer.helped grow Mecca’s economy: played a part in making the city’s business bigger
correctAnswer.allowed merchants to travel: made it possible for traders to go on journeys
correctAnswer.focused on worship: gave most of their attention to prayer and religious acts

languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Allow + person + to + verb” means “make something possible for someone”. “Focus on”, “show respect” and “stay away from” are fixed phrases: the small words (“on”, “from”) cannot be changed. Together they explain how agreements and the sacred months made trade and travel easier.

feedback.correct: Correct. You matched each phrase with its meaning in the chapter.
feedback.incorrect: Read the second and third paragraphs of Chapter 5 again and replace each phrase with your answer. Does the sentence still make sense?

languageFocusExercises.title: Time, Result and Purpose
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Choose the correct form to complete each sentence from Chapter 5.
languageFocusExercises.question: Which form marks a starting time, a new state and a purpose?

formChoices.sentence: [choice] the early 6th century, Mecca became a major trading center.
The sacred months, Dhu al-Qadah, Dhu al-Hijjah, Muharram, and Rajab, made the region [choice].
… more people could visit the city [choice] Hajj.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: “From + time” marks the point where a change began, and it works with the past simple (“became”). “Since” would need the present perfect or past perfect. “Make + object + adjective” describes a new state: “made the region safer” (no “to be”, and “safer” already means “more safe”). “To + verb” gives the purpose of a visit.

feedback.correct: Correct. You marked the starting time, the new state and the purpose.
feedback.incorrect: Check the verb in the first sentence (“became”), remember that “safer” is already a comparative, and ask why people visited. Then compare with Chapter 5.

languageFocusExercises.title: Explain How Conditions Create Opportunity

pages.title: Fairs and Wealth
pages.content:
Before Islam, idol worshippers continued to visit and walk around the Ka’ba. They also ran between Safa and Marwa and stood in Arafat. These practices kept Mecca active during the pilgrimage season.

This religious activity also helped business grow quickly. Big trade fairs such as Ukaz, Majannah, and Dhul-Majaz took place during this time. People attended these fairs first and then went to Arafat.

At the beginning of the 7th century, the Quraysh tribe controlled the most important trade routes and wealth in Arabia. The Quraysh used gold and silver coins for trade. In the city, lending money with usury was widespread. This made the rich richer and the poor poorer.

exercises.title: Pilgrims and Business
exercises.instructions: Read the question. Choose the answer from Chapter 6.
exercises.question: Why did business grow quickly in Mecca during the pilgrimage season?
options: Many people came for religious practices, and big trade fairs took place at the same time.
Lending money with usury was not allowed during the pilgrimage season, so prices were fair.
People went to Arafat first, so the fairs were empty and prices were very low in the city.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 6 says the pilgrimage practices “kept Mecca active during the pilgrimage season. This religious activity also helped business grow quickly. Big trade fairs such as Ukaz, Majannah, and Dhul-Majaz took place during this time.” People attended the fairs first and then went to Arafat.

feedback.correct: Correct. Religious activity and the big fairs came together, so business grew quickly.
feedback.incorrect: Read the first two paragraphs of Chapter 6. What kept Mecca active, and what took place “during this time”?

languageFocusExercises.title: What Does “Continued To” Show?
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Read the sentence from Chapter 6. Is the statement true or false?
languageFocusExercises.question: “Before Islam, idol worshippers continued to visit and walk around the Ka’ba.” The words “continued to” show that visiting the Ka’ba was a new practice that started at this time.
languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Continue to + verb” shows that an action went on and did not stop. People had already visited the Ka’ba for a long time (Chapter 3: “the Ka’ba became a pilgrimage site”). Even after people started worshipping idols, the visits did not stop. The writer then shows the effect of this continuing activity on the city.

feedback.correct: Correct. “Continued to” describes an old practice that did not stop.
feedback.incorrect: Think about the difference between “started to” and “continued to”. Then remember when the Ka’ba first became a pilgrimage site.

languageFocusExercises.title: Find and Fix the Mistake
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Each sentence has one mistake. Tap the wrong word or phrase, then choose the correction.
languageFocusExercises.question: Can you fix the verbs after “kept” and “helped”?

errorItems.sentence: These practices kept Mecca to be active during the pilgrimage season.
This religious activity also helped business growing quickly.
People attended these fairs first and then go to Arafat.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Keep + object + adjective” shows that a situation stays the same: “kept Mecca active”. “Help + object + base verb” shows support for a change: “helped business grow”. “First … and then …” orders two past actions, so both verbs are in the past simple: “attended … and then went”.

feedback.correct: Well done. You fixed the verb patterns and the sequence.
feedback.incorrect: Check the first two paragraphs of Chapter 6: what comes after “kept Mecca”, after “helped business”, and after “then”?

languageFocusExercises.title: Richer and Poorer
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Tap the pieces to rebuild the last sentence of Chapter 6.
languageFocusExercises.question: How can one sentence show a practice pushing two groups in opposite directions?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Make + object + comparative adjective” shows how something changed a group: “made the rich richer”. After “and”, the writer does not repeat “made”; the second group simply follows the same pattern: “and the poor poorer”. “This” refers back to lending money with usury.

feedback.correct: Well done. Each group is followed by the comparative that shows how it changed.
feedback.incorrect: Start with “This made”, then give a group and how it changed, then “and”, then the other group. Check the last paragraph of Chapter 6.

languageFocusExercises.title: Explain a System and Its Effects

feedback.correct: Keep the paragraph connected and make each form express a real relationship between ideas.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 2 — Explain what that activity “kept” active, busy, open or connected.

pages.title: Rich and Poor
pages.content:
Usury caused a big gap between social classes. Powerful people were usually merchants who lent money with usury. Many people were in debt and could not pay back their debts because of high interest. Drinking and gambling were also common, and these habits often pushed people deeper into debt.

While the rich lived in luxury with gold plates and silver cups, the poor struggled to survive. For the wealthy Quraysh, money and tribe were the most important values.

When Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) started calling people to Islam, some rich leaders asked why Muhammad should be the leader while they were rich and important. Orphans and weak people were treated badly, and powerful people often took their property by force.

languageFocusExercises.title: Whose Idea Is It?
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Read the sentence from Chapter 7. Then choose the best answer.
languageFocusExercises.question: “When Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) started calling people to Islam, some rich leaders asked why Muhammad should be the leader while they were rich and important.” What does this reported question show?
options: The writer thinks that rich and important people should be the leaders of the city.
The leaders wanted information about the Prophet’s life, so they asked him real questions.
The leaders were objecting: They thought money and status should decide who leads.
The leaders agreed that Muhammad should be the leader, but they asked about his plans.
languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Asked why …” reports a question, but here the question is really an objection. The words “while they were rich and important” show the leaders’ own view: Wealth and status should give power. The writer reports this view; he does not agree with it. This fits the chapter’s picture of a society where wealth and tribe decided a person’s value.

feedback.correct: Correct. The reported question shows the leaders’ objection, not the writer’s opinion.
feedback.incorrect: Look at who is asking and at the words “while they were rich and important”. Is this the writer speaking, or the leaders?

languageFocusExercises.title: Contrast and Importance
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Rewrite each sentence so that it keeps the same meaning. Use the start that is given.
languageFocusExercises.question: Can you move a “while” contrast and say “the most important” in a different way?

transformItems.source: While the rich lived in luxury with gold plates and silver cups, the poor struggled to survive.
transformItems.frame: The poor struggled to survive, [blank] in luxury with gold plates and silver cups.

transformItems.source: For the wealthy Quraysh, money and tribe were the most important values.
transformItems.frame: For the wealthy Quraysh, nothing was more important than [blank].

languageFocusExercises.explanation: “While” can join two situations that exist at the same time and show how different they are. The “while” clause can come first or second. A superlative (“the most important”) can also be expressed with “nothing was more important than …”. Both forms help the writer show the values of one group very clearly.

feedback.correct: Well done. You kept the contrast and the meaning of the superlative.
feedback.incorrect: Item 1: start the gap with “while” and describe the rich. Item 2: what did the wealthy Quraysh value most? Check the second paragraph of Chapter 7.

languageFocusExercises.title: Why Debt Grew
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Complete the lines from Chapter 7 with words from the bank. Two words are not needed.

languageFocusExercises.fillBlanksText: Many people were in debt and [blank] pay back their debts [blank] high interest. Drinking and gambling were also common, and these habits often pushed people deeper [blank] debt.
languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Could not + verb” shows that people were unable to do something. “Because of” + noun phrase (high interest) gives the cause; “because” would need a subject and verb. “Push + person + into” shows movement into a worse situation, and “deeper” shows that the situation became more serious.

feedback.correct: Correct. You showed the inability, its cause and the worsening result.
feedback.incorrect: Look at what follows each gap: A verb, a noun phrase, or the word “debt” after “deeper”. Then check the first paragraph of Chapter 7.

pages.title: Tribal Life
pages.content:
Tribes were the center of Arab society. Life in the desert was very hard, so physical strength was extremely important. Men were often seen as valuable because they were fighters in wars.

To earn respect from other tribes, families wanted to have many sons. Without a tribe, people could not easily protect their lives or property. A person outside tribal protection was in great danger.

Early Arabs were highly proud of their ancestors and remembered their names carefully. The most important rule was to work for the tribe and follow it. They had to protect and honor their tribe in every situation, even when the tribe did something wrong.

exercises.title: Loyal in Every Situation
exercises.instructions: Is the sentence true or false? Use Chapter 8.

exercises.explanation: Chapter 8 says people “had to protect and honor their tribe in every situation, even when the tribe did something wrong.” So loyalty to the tribe could come before justice.

feedback.correct: Correct. People had to support their tribe even when it did wrong, so loyalty could come before justice.
feedback.incorrect: Read the last sentence of Chapter 8 and look at the words “in every situation, even when …”.

languageFocusExercises.title: Words for Loyalty and Duty
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Match each phrase from Chapter 8 with its meaning.
languageFocusExercises.question: What do these phrases tell us about duties and pride in tribal life?

matchingPairs.right: felt great honor because of their family line

matchingPairs.left: They had to protect … their tribe
matchingPairs.right: it was their duty to defend their group
whatever happened, at all times

matchingPairs.left: even when the tribe did something wrong
matchingPairs.right: also in cases where their group was at fault

languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Had to” expresses a strong duty or obligation. “In every situation” makes the duty general. “Even when” adds a case where we would not expect the duty to continue; it shows how strong tribal loyalty was. “Outside” here means “not covered by” tribal protection.

feedback.correct: Correct. You matched each phrase with its meaning in tribal life.
feedback.incorrect: Read the second and third paragraphs of Chapter 8 again. Replace each phrase with your answer and check that the sentence still makes sense.

languageFocusExercises.title: Result, Reason, Purpose
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Complete the lines from Chapter 8 with words from the bank. Two words are not needed.
languageFocusExercises.question: Which word gives a result, which gives a reason, and which gives a purpose?
languageFocusExercises.fillBlanksText: Life in the desert was very hard, [blank] physical strength was extremely important. Men were often seen as valuable [blank] they were fighters in wars. [blank] earn respect from other tribes, families wanted to have many sons.
languageFocusExercises.explanation: “So” introduces a result (hard life → strength was important). “Because” + subject + verb gives a reason (why were men valued?). “To + verb” at the start of a sentence gives the purpose of the action that follows (why did families want many sons?). “For” and “because of” cannot be followed by a verb here.

feedback.correct: Correct. You chose the right link for result, reason and purpose.
feedback.incorrect: For each gap, ask: Is this a result, a reason, or the aim of an action? Then check the first two paragraphs of Chapter 8.

languageFocusExercises.title: “Without” and “If”
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Rewrite the sentence from Chapter 8 with “if”. Keep the same meaning.
languageFocusExercises.question: How can we say “without …” with “if”?

transformItems.source: Without a tribe, people could not easily protect their lives or property.
transformItems.frame: If people did not have a tribe, they [blank] their lives or property.
answers: were not able to easily protect
were not easily able to protect

languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Without + noun” is a short way to express a condition: “without a tribe” = “if people did not have a tribe”. “Could not easily” shows limited ability: Protection was very difficult, not simply impossible. That is why the next sentence says a person outside tribal protection was “in great danger”.

feedback.correct: Well done. You turned the “without” phrase into a condition and kept the limited ability.
feedback.incorrect: Keep “could not” and the word “easily” in your answer. Check the second paragraph of Chapter 8.

languageFocusExercises.title: Explain Rules, Support and Consequences

pages.title: Women, Slavery and Poetry
pages.content:
Before Islam, the life of Arab women was very different depending on their wealth and family. Rich women, like Khadija, could run their own businesses. However, many poor women had no rights and faced unfair treatment. Some fathers were ashamed to have daughters because they wanted sons to increase their power in society.

In old Mecca, slavery was an ordinary part of the economy. Slaves lived in very cruel conditions and were bought and sold like animals. They did the most difficult work, and owning many slaves was a sign of wealth.

Poets were also very important in social life. Poetry kept tribal history alive, praised tribes, and criticized enemies. In those days, poets were like the media of the people.

vocabulary.definition: __historical_entity__:mecca-mecca-7th-century
Basic freedoms and fair treatment that people should have.
Behavior that is not just or equal.
A system in which people are owned and forced to work.
People who write or perform poetry.
Ways of sharing news, ideas, and messages with people.

hotspots.title: Status of Women

exercises.title: Different Lives
exercises.instructions: Read the question. Choose the answer from Chapter 9.
exercises.question: Why could Khadija run her own business when many poor women had no rights?
options: She was a famous poet, and poets were very important in social life.
A woman’s life depended on her wealth and family, and Khadija was rich.
She had many sons, and in that society sons brought a family respect.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 9 says “the life of Arab women was very different depending on their wealth and family. Rich women, like Khadija, could run their own businesses. However, many poor women had no rights.”

feedback.correct: Right. Wealth and family made the difference: Rich women like Khadija had chances that poor women did not have.
feedback.incorrect: Read the first two sentences of Chapter 9. What made the lives of Arab women so different?

languageFocusExercises.title: What Does “Depending On” Mean?
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Read the sentence from Chapter 9. Is the statement true or false?
languageFocusExercises.question: “Before Islam, the life of Arab women was very different depending on their wealth and family.” This means that a woman’s life changed according to how rich she was and which family she came from.
languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Depending on …” shows that one thing changes according to another factor. Here, women’s lives changed according to wealth and family. The next sentences give the two sides: What rich women like Khadija were able to do, and then, marked by “However”, the situation of many poor women.

feedback.correct: Correct. “Depending on” tells us what made the difference between women’s lives.
feedback.incorrect: Read the next two sentences of Chapter 9. Were the lives of a rich woman and a poor woman the same or different? What made the difference?

languageFocusExercises.title: Who Did It?
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Rewrite each part of Chapter 9. Use the start that is given.
languageFocusExercises.question: Why does the chapter keep the slaves, not the owners, at the center of these sentences?

transformItems.source: Slaves lived in very cruel conditions and were bought and sold like animals.
transformItems.frame: Slaves lived in very cruel conditions, and people [blank] like animals.

transformItems.source: They did the most difficult work, and owning many slaves was a sign of wealth.
transformItems.frame: They did the most difficult work, and if someone [blank], it was a sign of wealth.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: The passive “were bought and sold” keeps the slaves as the subject, so the reader stays focused on what happened to them; the people who did it are not important for the point. In your active version the subject is only “people”. An -ing form (“owning many slaves”) can be the subject of a sentence; it names an action as one idea.

feedback.correct: Well done. You changed the focus of each sentence and kept the meaning.
feedback.incorrect: Item 1: use the active verbs “bought and sold” and put the slaves after them. Item 2: after “if someone”, use a past simple verb. Check the second paragraph of Chapter 9.

languageFocusExercises.title: Find and Fix the Mistake
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Each sentence has one mistake. Tap the wrong word or phrase, then choose the correction.
languageFocusExercises.question: Can you fix the verbs in these sentences?

errorItems.sentence: Rich women, like Khadija, could ran their own businesses.
Some fathers were ashamed to have daughters because of they wanted sons to increase their power in society.
Poetry kept tribal history alive, praised tribes, and criticizing enemies.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: After “could”, use the base verb: “could run”. “Because” + subject + verb gives a reason; “because of” needs a noun. In a list of actions, every verb has the same form: “kept …, praised …, and criticized …”. This parallel list lets the writer show three jobs of poetry in one clear sentence.

feedback.correct: Well done. You fixed the modal verb, the reason clause and the parallel list.
feedback.incorrect: Check the first paragraph of Chapter 9 for the first two sentences, and the last paragraph for the list of what poetry did.

languageFocusExercises.title: Describe Unequal Roles and Social Functions
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Write or say six sentences about people in a community, then or now.
languageFocusExercises.question: Who had more chances, and who had fewer?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: A strong response should use language such as “depending on...”, “however”, “because”, a passive form, and a clear list of parallel verbs or a useful comparison.

feedback.correct: Keep the ideas connected so the grammar shows real relationships rather than appearing as separate examples.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 1 — Say how chances were different “depending on …”
discussionPrompts.example: In many villages long ago, children’s chances were very different depending on their family’s money.

discussionPrompts.example: Some parents kept their children at home because they needed help with the work.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 4 — Say what happened to people: “… were treated / helped / sent …”
discussionPrompts.example: Poor workers were often paid very little and were sent away without warning.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 5 — Say two or three things a place or group did.
discussionPrompts.example: The village school taught children, gave them a hot meal and helped them make friends.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 6 — Compare it: “It was like …”

pages.title: Religious Life in Mecca
pages.content:
Before Islam, most people in Arabia worshipped idols. Only a few people followed religions like Christianity. In Mecca, most people also worshipped idols. There were 360 idols, including Lat, Manat, and Uzza. They were kept in and around the Ka’ba and in homes.

Some people, called Hanifs, followed the old religion of Abraham (pbuh). Arab people in that period actually believed in one main God, Allah, as the Creator. However, they also worshipped many idols. They thought these idols helped them talk to Allah.

Pilgrimage to the Ka’ba was the most important religious activity in early Arabia. Life in the Age of Ignorance was also full of superstitions. People believed in kahins, or soothsayers, and checked omens before making decisions.

vocabulary.definition: __historical_entity__:mecca-mecca-7th-century
__historical_entity__:mecca-arabian-peninsula
__historical_entity__:mecca-kaaba-7th-century
Objects wrongly worshipped as gods.
People who followed the old religion of Abraham (pbuh) and did not worship idols.
Allah, the One who created everything.
Beliefs based on fear or tradition rather than sound evidence or true religion.
Signs people believed could predict what would happen.

hotspots.title: 360 Idols
hotspots.description: 360 idols, including Lat, Manat and Uzza, were kept in and around the Ka’ba and in homes.

hotspots.title: Hanifs
hotspots.description: Hanifs followed the old religion of Abraham (pbuh) rather than idol worship.

exercises.title: Allah and the Idols
exercises.instructions: Read the question. Choose the answer from Chapter 10.
exercises.question: Many Arabs believed in Allah as the Creator. Why did they also worship idols?
options: They thought the idols had created the world.
They wanted to check omens before making decisions.
They thought the idols helped them talk to Allah.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 10 says Arab people “actually believed in one main God, Allah, as the Creator. However, they also worshipped many idols. They thought these idols helped them talk to Allah.” Omens are mentioned too, but as a superstition, not as the reason for the idols.

feedback.correct: Correct. They saw the idols as a way to reach Allah, even though they believed Allah was the Creator.
feedback.incorrect: Read the second paragraph of Chapter 10. Find the sentence after “However, they also worshipped many idols.”

languageFocusExercises.title: Fact or Belief?
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Does the writer say it, or report what people then believed? Sort the parts.
languageFocusExercises.question: Which parts are facts, and which are old beliefs?

items: Pilgrimage to the Ka’ba was the most important religious activity in early Arabia.
Life in the Age of Ignorance was also full of superstitions.

dragDropGroups.group: The writer reports what people thought or believed
items: They thought these idols helped them talk to Allah.
People believed in kahins, or soothsayers …
Arab people in that period actually believed in one main God, Allah, as the Creator.

The writer says it directly: Pilgrimage to the Ka’ba was the most important religious activity in early Arabia.
Life in the Age of Ignorance was also full of superstitions.
The writer reports what people thought o: They thought these idols helped them talk to Allah.
People believed in kahins, or soothsayers …
Arab people in that period actually believed in one main God, Allah, as the Creator.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Thought” and “believed (in)” report what people in the past accepted as true. They do not mean that the writer agrees: “They thought these idols helped them talk to Allah” is their belief, not a fact. Sentences without a reporting verb are the writer’s own statements, including judgements like “full of superstitions”.

feedback.correct: Correct. You separated the writer’s own statements from reported beliefs.
feedback.incorrect: Look for “thought” and “believed”. If one of these verbs is present, the sentence reports people’s beliefs.

languageFocusExercises.title: How Many People?
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Choose the correct word to complete each sentence from Chapter 10.
languageFocusExercises.question: Which words describe a large group, a small group and examples inside a group accurately?

formChoices.sentence: Before Islam, [choice] people in Arabia worshipped idols.
There were 360 idols, [choice] Lat, Manat, and Uzza.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Most” means the majority, not everyone; “all” would be an overclaim because the next sentence names people who followed other religions. “Only a few” is used with countable nouns such as “people”; “a little” is for uncountable nouns. “Including” introduces some examples from a larger group; it does not give the full list.

feedback.correct: Correct. You described the groups accurately without overgeneralising.
feedback.incorrect: Ask: Did everyone worship idols? Is “people” countable? Does the list give all 360 idols or only some examples? Then check the first paragraph of Chapter 10.

languageFocusExercises.title: Where and When
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Rewrite each sentence so that it keeps the same meaning. Use the start that is given.
languageFocusExercises.question: How else can we say where and when?

transformItems.source: They were kept in and around the Ka’ba and in homes.
transformItems.frame: People [blank] in and around the Ka’ba and in homes.

transformItems.source: People believed in kahins, or soothsayers, and checked omens before making decisions.
transformItems.frame: … and checked omens before they [blank].

languageFocusExercises.explanation: The chapter uses the passive “were kept” because the idols and their places are the topic; who kept them is not important. “Before + -ing” is a short form of “before + subject + verb”: “before making decisions” = “before they made decisions”. It shows that checking omens came first and the decision came after.

feedback.correct: Well done. You changed the focus and the time clause without changing the meaning.
feedback.incorrect: Item 1: use the past simple “kept” and put the idols after it. Item 2: use a past simple verb after “before they”.

languageFocusExercises.title: Describe Beliefs Without Overgeneralizing
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Write or say six sentences about what people in a community believe.
languageFocusExercises.question: What did most people believe, and who was different?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: A strong response should use precise group language such as “most”, “some” or “only a few”, plus a passive form, reported belief, and a clear before/decision relationship.

feedback.correct: Keep the sentences connected so each language choice helps explain a real relationship.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 1 — Give the main group with “most”.
discussionPrompts.example: In my grandparents’ village, most people were farmers.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 2 — Add a few different people: “Only a few …” or “Some …”
discussionPrompts.example: Only a few people worked in the town.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 3 — Say where something was: “… was found / kept / placed in …”
discussionPrompts.example: Small “lucky” stones were found in many homes.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 4 — Say what a group thought or believed.
discussionPrompts.example: People thought that these stones brought good weather for the crops.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 5 — Say what they did before a decision: “Before …ing, …”
discussionPrompts.example: Before planting the seeds, the farmers looked at the sky for signs.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 6 — Say how the belief changed what they did.
discussionPrompts.example: This belief made them wait for a “lucky” day, even when the soil was ready.

pages.title: What Islam Meant
pages.content:
Politics, economics, and religion are connected. Beliefs shape how people live. That is why powerful groups in Mecca did not like Islam. From the beginning, Islam showed that Muslims were a new community. They were going to be different from the people around them.

In 610, Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) started teaching Islam in Mecca. The Quraysh tribe heard his message first. Some people became Muslims. When they heard Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) read the Qur’an, they were sure it was from Allah.

This message changed them deeply. It touched their hearts and minds and made them feel great respect. However, many leaders ignored the Qur’an and stood against the Prophet (pbuh). Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) taught in Mecca for 13 years, in a city with about 5,000 to 10,000 people.

vocabulary.definition: __historical_entity__:mecca-mecca-7th-century
__historical_entity__:mecca-quraysh
Activities connected with power and governing society.
Activities connected with money, work, trade, and resources.
A group of people who share a common life or identity.
Refused to pay attention to something.
People who guide or have authority over a group.

hotspots.title: A New Community
hotspots.description: Islam formed a new community with beliefs that differed from the society around it.

hotspots.title: The Qur’an
hotspots.description: The message of the Qur’an deeply affected those who accepted it, while many leaders opposed it.

exercises.title: Why Powerful Groups Worried
exercises.instructions: Read the question. Choose the answer from Chapter 11.
exercises.question: Why did powerful groups in Mecca not like Islam?
options: Beliefs shape how people live, so a new religion could change life and power in the city.
The Quraysh tribe was the last group in Mecca to hear the message, so they felt left out.
Islam asked Muslims to stay the same as the people around them and to keep the old customs.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 11 begins: “Politics, economics, and religion are connected. Beliefs shape how people live. That is why powerful groups in Mecca did not like Islam.” The Quraysh heard the message first, and Muslims were going to be different from the people around them.

feedback.correct: Right. Because religion is connected with politics and economics, a new belief could change who had power.
feedback.incorrect: Read the first paragraph of Chapter 11 and find the words “That is why …”. What do the sentences before them say?

languageFocusExercises.title: What Does “That Is Why” Connect?
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Read the start of Chapter 11. Then choose the best answer.
languageFocusExercises.question: “Politics, economics, and religion are connected. Beliefs shape how people live. That is why powerful groups in Mecca did not like Islam.” What does “That is why” do here?
options: It gives the reason why politics, economics and religion are connected: Powerful groups in Mecca did not like Islam.
It shows that the leaders’ dislike of Islam was a result of the ideas before it: A new belief could change how people live, and so affect power and wealth too.
It introduces an example of a new belief that changed how the people of Mecca lived, traded and worshipped.
It shows a contrast with the sentence before it: Beliefs shape how people live, but the leaders did not care about beliefs.
languageFocusExercises.explanation: “That is why” points back to the ideas already given and introduces their result. The writer first makes two general statements (in the present simple because they are always true) and then applies them to history (in the past simple). A new belief could change how people lived, and so it could also change who had power and money.

feedback.correct: Correct. The dislike of Islam is presented as a result of the general ideas before it.
feedback.incorrect: “That” refers back to what came before. Ask: Is the last sentence a reason, an example, a contrast, or a result?

languageFocusExercises.title: Looking Forward from the Past
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Choose the correct form to complete each sentence from Chapter 11.
languageFocusExercises.question: Which forms show a future development seen from the past, and an action someone heard?

formChoices.sentence: From the beginning, Islam showed that Muslims were a new community. They [choice] different from the people around them.
When they heard Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) [choice] the Qur’an, they were sure it was from Allah.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Was/were going to + verb” describes a future development seen from a point in the past: at the beginning, the difference was still to come. “They” is plural, so “were”. “Hear + person + base verb” reports an action that someone heard from start to end: “heard Prophet Muhammad read the Qur’an” (no “to”, and no -s).

feedback.correct: Correct. You chose the future-in-the-past and the right verb after “heard”.
feedback.incorrect: The story is told in the past, and “they” is plural. After “heard + person”, use the base verb. Check the first two paragraphs of Chapter 11.

languageFocusExercises.title: Effect, Contrast and Time
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Complete the lines from Chapter 11 with words from the bank. Three words are not needed.
languageFocusExercises.question: Which words show an effect on people, a contrast between reactions, and a length of time?
languageFocusExercises.fillBlanksText: This message changed them deeply. It touched their hearts and minds and made them [blank] great respect. [blank], many leaders ignored the Qur’an and stood against the Prophet (pbuh). Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) taught in Mecca [blank] 13 years, in a city with about 5,000 to 10,000 people.
languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Make + person + base verb” shows an effect on someone’s feelings: “made them feel great respect” (no “to”). “However” introduces a reaction that is the opposite of the one before; “So” would wrongly present the leaders’ opposition as a result of the message touching people’s hearts. “For + a period of time” gives the length of time; “since” needs a starting point.

feedback.correct: Correct. You showed the effect, the contrasting reaction and the length of time.
feedback.incorrect: Check the last paragraph of Chapter 11. After “made them”, is there “to”? Do the leaders react in the same way or the opposite way? Is “13 years” a length or a starting point?

languageFocusExercises.title: Explain a Social Change
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Write or say six sentences about a change at school, at home or in a community.
languageFocusExercises.question: How did a new idea change people?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: A strong answer should include a general relationship, a clear cause/result link, a new group identity or role, one “was/were going to” sentence, a time clause with “when”, and a contrast with “however”.

feedback.correct: Keep the six sentences connected so the reader can follow the change and the different reactions.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 1 — State how two parts of the situation are connected.
discussionPrompts.example: At our school, sport and health are closely connected.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 2 — Explain how an idea or belief affected behavior.
discussionPrompts.example: When students learned about healthy food, many of them changed what they ate.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 3 — Use “That is why” to show a result or reaction.
discussionPrompts.example: That is why the school café stopped selling sugary drinks.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 4 — Describe a new identity, role or community.
discussionPrompts.example: The students in the new healthy-eating club became a team that helped the whole school.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 5 — Use “was/were going to” for a later development viewed from the past.
discussionPrompts.example: They were going to teach younger students about good food the next year.

discussionPrompts.question: Sentence 6 — Use “When...” and “However...” to compare two reactions.
discussionPrompts.example: When the parents heard about the change, most of them were happy. However, some students were angry because they liked the old drinks.

beforeYouRead.quote: Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) taught in Mecca for 13 years

I can show a result with “That is why”.
I can explain a change and two different reactions to it.

pages.title: The Leaders of Quraysh
pages.content:
In the first few years of the call to Islam, almost none of Mecca’s super-rich people became Muslims. The leaders of Quraysh felt that Islam was a danger to their power and did not accept it.

They were very rich, and other tribes respected them because of trade and the idols in the Ka’ba. They had high prestige. This made them the prestigious caretakers of pilgrimage in the Arabian region. Keeping their power and unity was very important for them. Rich leaders turned the people against the new religion.

Islam brought serious changes. For example, Quraysh used unfair money systems like usury, but the Qur’an forbade this and allowed only honest trade. Islam also commanded zakat and sadaqah to help the poor. Meccan leaders tried to stop Islam from growing.

vocabulary.definition: __historical_entity__:mecca-mecca-7th-century
__historical_entity__:mecca-kaaba-7th-century
__historical_entity__:mecca-quraysh
Extremely wealthy.
Highly respected and admired.
People responsible for looking after a place or activity.
Did not allow something.
Obligatory charity that Muslims give under Islamic rules.
Being together as one group.

hotspots.title: Quraysh Leaders
hotspots.description: The leaders of Quraysh saw Islam as a danger to their power and status.

hotspots.title: Honest Trade
hotspots.description: The Qur’an forbade usury and allowed honest trade, while Islam commanded support for the poor.

matchingHeadings.right: What the chapter says about it

exercises.title: Power and Change
exercises.instructions: Match each idea with what Chapter 12 says about it.
exercises.question: What does Chapter 12 say about the Quraysh leaders and the changes Islam brought?

matchingPairs.right: a danger to their power

matchingPairs.left: Trade and the idols in the Ka’ba
